title: Model-specific outlier handling & layer-wise scaling for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: implement model-specific outlier detection and layer-wise scaling adjustments in the FP8/INT8 calibration pipeline to prevent per-layer activation collapse and to preserve generation quality across LLama, Mistral, and Qwen families. Deliverables: (1) a calibration pass that outputs per-layer scale/bias overrides and per-channel clipping thresholds; (2) an evaluation harness to validate bleu/commensurate MMLU/PIQA rerun against float baselines; (3) runtime config keys to load profile overrides and to enable fallback to higher-precision layers at serving time.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration pipeline produces per-layer JSON profile that reduces LM perplexity delta vs fp32 to <= 2% on validation prompts for each model family. 2) INT8/FP8 quantized model with layer-wise scaling fixes shows no >3% drop in task-level metrics (tech-document summarization, MMLU subset) compared to baseline. 3) Runtime can accept profile overrides via model metadata and fall back to mixed-precision for problematic layers at inference without restarting nodes.
implementation_notes: - Split calibration into two passes: a lightweight statistical pass (collect per-channel mean/var, extreme percentiles) followed by a targeted AD outlier pass using trimmed-moments on activations. - Introduce 'layer_bias' and 'clip_threshold' fields in quant profiles. - For Qwen, pay attention to its RMS-norm scaling behavior; use multiplicative rescaling instead of additive bias for normed layers. - Mistral: detect early-attention-heads with heavy tail activations and apply head-wise clipping. - Llama: older versions need per-embedding-table special handling to avoid embedding overflow. - Add a small validation corpus (~2000 prompts) covering code, math, instruction, and dialogue to capture sensitivity to calibration decisions.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed—collected activation histograms for llama-3-8b, mistral-7b, qwen-7b. Observed layer 24/attn for Mistral and layer 12/ffn for Qwen with extreme 0.01% tails.

2026-02-28: Prototype calibration pass merged on branch feat/quant-calib-spike (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147). Produces per-layer percentiles and suggested clip thresholds.
2026-03-03: First accuracy runs: INT8 baseline without layer fixes shows 8-12% task metric drop on Mistral prompts. FP8 baseline better but unstable for certain tokenization patterns.
2026-03-07: Implemented layer-wise multiplicative rescaling and head-wise clipping. Added model-family switch in calibration (--family llama|mistral|qwen).

2026-03-10: Validation harness extended. Running batch jobs to compute perplexity and MMLU subset. Early results: Mistral with head-wise clipping reduces metric drop to 2.5% in INT8; Qwen needs per-embedding table clamp to reach similar numbers.
2026-03-12: Code review feedback requested more unit tests for the new profile loader and a runtime safety switch to force fallback on >5% metric deltas reported by live canary. Assigned follow-ups.
Next steps: finish unit tests, add telemetry for 'profile_applied' and 'fallback_triggered', finalize release notes for runtime-2.4.
review_feedback: Design review (Mar 05) - Sofia Ramirez: suggested adding per-channel symmetric/asymmetric choice and documenting tradeoffs in the PRD.
Engineering review (Mar 11) - Noah Patel: asked to ensure that profile overrides are backwards compatible and that missing fields default to safe conservative values.
PM sign-off pending additional accuracy runs on the 'instruction' slice (Priya Kapoor).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive clipping may reduce hallucination but increase tokenization artifacts (broken subword probabilities). Mitigation: use holdout prompt set and prefer multiplicative rescale where possible.
Risk: Qwen embedding overflow on INT8 path. Mitigation: keep embeddings in FP16 or enable per-table mixed-precision flag in profile.
Risk: runtime perf regressions from extra per-layer checks. Mitigation: cache applied profiles and only evaluate fallback heuristics at configured intervals.
Risk: calibration profiles may overfit to our validation corpus. Mitigation: use cross-model holdout and random prompt augmentation during calibration.
Operational risk: canary could trigger rollbacks frequently. Mitigation: add hysteresis and require sustained metric degradation across 3 windows before automatic rollback.
manual_steps: Checkout feat/quant-calib branch, run `python -m quant.calibrate --model <model> --out profile.json --family mistral` to generate a profile.
Run validation: `python -m eval.run --profile profile.json --tasks mmmluu_subset,piqa --out results.json`
To test runtime: load model with --profile-overrides profile.json and run canary traffic via /internal/canary endpoint.
